doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: Jam cruise with Maceo Parker, Fred Wesley and Pee Wee Ellis
summary: Playing alongside Maceo Parker, Fred Wesley and Pee Wee Ellis, who taught arrangements.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah. We tend to not want to think about those things. How about the best thing you’ve ever done? I mean is it possible to highlight a few?

Well you mean — just recently one of the greatest, yeah, we did the jam cruise which was last year, and I got to play with Maceo Parker, Fred Wesley and Pee Wee Ellis, on stage, right next to me. If you go, there’s pictures on Facebook and stuff, but what an honor that was, to be side by side with Pee Wee and like I said Maceo and Fred Wesley, was crazy. And we just got to do that again in New Orleans as well. Alfred Ellis, what a great guy he is, and he taught us a lot too. Me and Ryan Zorcas got to hang out with him a lot and Pee Wee taught us arrangements for us for these jazz round tunes that he wrote himself, like in “I Feel Good” and stuff that he actually wrote. That was, playing that gig was like, wow, definitely one of the highlights. © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-
You know it’s hard to put into words the way those guys play those horn parts. There’s something about it that’s just so cool.

Maceo alone, Jeez. When you’ve seen him live, it’s like when you just played Cannonball, it goes right to your bones, it just goes right in there. I don’t know how to explain it, but just to be around him was quite an experience.
